house_note: This file audits the audit. Every limit names the modality that was not run, the concern classes whose confidence it bounds, and the cheapest closure. Absence of a finding in a class below is reported as absence, never as a clean bill. Tags: [measured] = computed or read by this critic from the audit's own artifacts or the repo; [documented] = stated by the orchestrator brief or a live source; [inferred] = reasoned.

limits.limit: Nothing was compiled. The Rust design's realisability -- five sync port traits held as dyn objects, an explicit cancel handle, the rk-kernel/rk-ports/rk-types layering -- was judged by reading design, ADRs and the spike runner's source, with rustc 1.97.1 installed on the box and crates/ empty.

evidence.quote: rustc/cargo 1.97.1 installed matches the pin
Five named ports, sync traits, async in adapters | **DECIDED** | Native async-fn-in-trait is **still not dyn-compatible**; `async_fn_in_dyn_trait` remains nightly-only.
`dispatch(ActivitySpec) -> Result<Typed, StepError>`; capability registry with dated probes; cost/usage; **`cancel(handle)`**
One trait per port; **no generic parameter bound by a port trait appears anywhere in the kernel**, and every port is held as one object-safe trait object | API-surface lint + a compile-fail

limits.consequence: Every B02-realisability verdict (14 findings, P1:3 -- L06-buildability-01 and -03 among them) and every 'no defect found' on trait shape in L06 (ADR-0076 layering vs the section 9.1 crate table; edition-2024 set_var; StepError variant census) is a reading-verdict with no compiler behind it. The design's own row 279 names 'a compile-fail' as the instrument for P1, and the audit never produced one. The one runtime measurement in this class is n=1 on one machine ('taskkill /T /F victim exit code = 1 on this Windows 11 box'). Confidence that Step 7a's trait can be written as ADR-0076 states it is [inferred], not [measured]; a shape the compiler rejects (object safety with an associated Typed, a cancel token that must be Send across the adapter runtime) would have been invisible to this audit.
limits.how_to_close: A named spike (ADR-0012 discharge, consumer RUNBOOK Step 7a): one throwaway crate of 50-150 lines under scratch, not crates/, declaring the five port traits as written in ADR-0076 and design section 3, one fake, a CancelToken, `traits.len() == fakes.len()`, and a `compile_fail` doctest for the generics-leak rule (design:279); `cargo check` on 1.97.1. Cost: 1-2 hours; zero corpus edits; the outcome is a spike file, and if it fails a successor to ADR-0076, never an edit.

limits.limit: No parser was written for the predicate grammar. Eight grammar ADRs (0033, 0034, 0035, 0040, 0048, 0049, 0069, 0070) were read for ambiguity; the only executable check of the grammar in the corpus is the P9 lint's R9, which is a regex vocabulary scan, not a parser, and precedence is undeclared by design.

evidence.quote: Predicate grammar (normative): roots are step inputs, facets, `rigor`, `item`; `.field` access; `len()`; `none/all/any(<field> in [...])` with the element's fields in scope; operators `== != < <= > >= in`; boolean connectives `and or not`; literals are string/number/bool/`null`. No user functions.
grouping is needed for readable `and`/`or` compositions without inventing precedence rules by convention
# --- R9 grammar + vocabulary
Read ADR-0031/0032/0033/0034/0040/0044/0046/0048/0049/0069/0070 in full plus schema 9a.1-7, 9b.18-19, 9c.39-40 and the P9 lint.py on_false handling.

evidence.file: grep -i precedence|associativ|EBNF over the eight grammar ADRs, design and AC register
evidence.quote: only hit inside the grammar ADRs is 0048:21 above; no precedence table, no associativity rule, no EBNF anywhere in the corpus

limits.consequence: B03-ambiguity's grammar findings and its absences are reading-only. Whether `not a and b or c`, a nested `any(... in ...)` inside `len()`, or a string literal containing `]` parses to one tree is not-answerable from the corpus as written, and the audit could not have found the cases a parser generator rejects. The corpus records the coalesce-chaining and null==non-null holes itself (L04: ALREADY-RECORDED); it does not record that the grammar has no precedence rule -- that is the class this modality would have surfaced. [inferred] Step 7b's lint author and the pack authors will infer precedence independently, which is exactly the two-implementer failure ADR-0033 was written to prevent.
limits.how_to_close: A named spike (consumer: RUNBOOK Step 7b lint, and a successor record to ADR-0033 if a precedence rule is needed): write the EBNF for ADR-0033+0048+0049+0070, a 150-250 line recursive-descent parser (Python is fine; it is throwaway), run it over every `applicable_if`/`require.when`/`on_false` string in spikes/p9 packs and catalog, and report the count that fail or parse two ways. Cost: 2-4 hours. Report as a count with its denominator, not as prose.

limits.limit: Wilson intervals were recomputed by one lens (L11) over 'every stated interval I could pair with a k/n', with partial independent recomputation in G01 (F36/F39), G02 (F40) and G15 (F29/F31). The pairing was manual; intervals whose k/n L11 could not locate were neither recomputed nor counted.

evidence.quote: Scripted (python, z=1.959964, plain Wilson) every stated interval I could pair with a k/n. MATCH to 2 dp, no defect
Wilson intervals recomputed independently
Wilson 0-14.3%, 0-27.8%, 33.0-70.8%, 22.2-59.2% all recompute: no defect

limits.consequence: B07-citation-statistics' 'no defect' on intervals holds for the paired set only; the unpaired residue has no number (not-measurable, not zero). The exact-McNemar and MCC checks for E3 were done once, by one script.
limits.how_to_close: Script: regex every `[a, b]` or `a-b%` bracket within 40 characters of a `k/n` or `k of n` in the four authority documents, FINDINGS.md and the F##-DRAFT files; recompute with Wilson, Wilson-cc and Clopper-Pearson; emit paired/unpaired/matched/mismatched counts. Cost: 1 hour. The unpaired count is the deliverable, whatever it is.

limits.limit: The 481-id design/register mirror diff (L12) ran over all 481 ids [measured], but it diffed four keyword classes only -- thresholds with units, comparator phrasings, state words, Instrument vs Verified-by -- and read by hand the 141 rows in the first class. Wording divergence of the GIVEN/WHEN/THEN body between a design mention and its register block was not diffed.

evidence.quote: Scripted over all 481 mirrored AC ids: 1,079 design mentions vs 514 register blocks ... 141 mention rows with unit-bearing numbers absent from the register block, all read ... 12 comparator phrasings beside an id: all agree. 27 state-word pairs near an id ... 79 Instrument-column vs Verified-by pairs: 12 keyword differences ... Checked 481 AC ids for threshold/Phase/state/instrument divergence: no defect found.

limits.consequence: 'No defect found' on the mirror is a no-defect on four keyword classes at full coverage, not on the criteria's semantics. A design row that narrows or widens an AC's WHEN clause without changing a number, a state word or the instrument column is outside what was checked. B04/B05-contradiction findings that touch AC wording came from area slices reading a sample, so the population rate of wording drift over 481 ids is not-measurable from this audit.
limits.how_to_close: Script: for each of the 481 ids, normalise the design sentence(s) carrying the id and the register block's GIVEN/WHEN/THEN, compute a token-set similarity, hand-read the lowest 50. Cost: 2 hours. Report the distribution, not a verdict.

limits.limit: The NEW / SHARPENS-KNOWN / ALREADY-RECORDED classification (174 / 161 / 3) rests on a keyword search_index over the 1,381 known-issues rows (about 15 keywords per row), queried by the finder and then by the refuter. A known row phrased in other vocabulary is missed and its finding counted NEW. The rows carry a source_anchor (file:line) that was not used for proximity matching.

evidence.quote: search_index: list 1381; sample entry {"id": "ARCH-0.1-001", "kind": "blocked_decision", "keywords": ["0.168", "200", "80%", "adr-0079", "p1", "context-vector", ...]}; rows[0].source_anchor = "references/2026-09-08-architecture-design.md:19"
Queried known-issues.json search_index for every finding (process group/job object/taskkill/143, handle, timeout, sqlite/busy_timeout, memo key/canonical ...)

limits.consequence: NEW is an upper bound; the direction of the error is one-way (a missed known row can only convert NEW to SHARPENS-KNOWN or ALREADY-RECORDED, never the reverse). The house rule 'never present a known item as a discovery' is therefore satisfied only to the recall of a keyword index whose recall was never measured. The 3 ALREADY-RECORDED survivors show the refuter did catch some; how many it did not is not-measurable.
limits.how_to_close: Script: for each of the 338 survivors, list every known-issues row whose source_anchor is in the same file within +/-5 lines of any finding anchor (1,420 anchors x 1,381 rows; trivial); hand-read the pairs for the 174 NEW. Cost: 30 minutes to script, 1-2 hours to read. Report the reclassification count.

what_the_numbers_rest_on.statement: In the corpus's own idiom: every count in this audit is a single pass by one model family on one day over one pin. 338 findings and 860 grounding verdicts are model-labelled with no human label file and no second draw; the only reproducibility figure is 9/9 on the census scripts, which measures the scripts, not the readers. Rates quoted about the audit (5.3% killed, 30.2% truth-WEAKENED) carry no interval because the process that produced them was run once and an interval over one run describes nothing. External verdicts are dated 2026-09-10 and are STALE-BY-DATE by construction from the next crates.io publish or docs change onward.

fault_names.saturated: not applicable to the audit's own rates -- nothing hit 0/n or n/n except the census reproducibility 9/9, which is a script property
fault_names.powerless: the killed-rate 19/357 and any per-lens finding count: n=1 run, no design could decide a hypothesis about them
fault_names.not_measurable: recall of any lens (PIA-M-12); keyword-index recall for NEW (PIA-M-08); wording-drift rate over 481 ids (PIA-M-04); residual body-vs-abstract risk over 83 preprints (PIA-M-09)
fault_names.not_answerable: whether the port traits compile (PIA-M-01) and whether the predicate grammar is unambiguous (PIA-M-02) -- the corpus as written does not contain the answer, and the audit did not build the instrument that would

ordering_for_the_deliverable: PIA-M-01 and PIA-M-02 are the two modalities whose absence can change what Step 5/7a/7b builds; both close in under half a day and each discharges as a named spike with a named consumer, which is the only form the corpus accepts for an unknown (ADR-0012).
PIA-M-05, PIA-M-06 and PIA-M-14 bound confidence in the priority ordering itself; PIA-M-08 bounds the NEW tag. These four should be stated at the head of the deliverable, before any concern.
PIA-M-03, PIA-M-04, PIA-M-07, PIA-M-09, PIA-M-10 bound specific classes and are each a one-to-three-hour script or fetch.
PIA-M-11, PIA-M-12, PIA-M-13 are hygiene of the audit record and cost nothing to state.
